document.title: PHOBOSIA Days 1-5 Mission, Screen, Interaction and Progression Specification
document.purpose: Implementation-ready source of truth for Phase 2. Attach this file to the coding-agent prompt and require the agent to inspect the repository and map these requirements onto the actual existing code and assets.
document.scope: Days 1-5 only, plus shared UI and mission foundations needed to support Days 6-14 later.
document.status: Design specification; not a claim that described features already exist.
document.important_note: Actual repository filenames, screen names, scene hierarchy, triggers, assets, transforms and visual references must be inspected before implementation. Do not invent file paths, assets, coordinates or existing object names.
priority: Preserve the existing Next.js + TypeScript + Three.js application.
Use the existing Master Terrain, selected location, coordinates, bounds, scale, exports, modules, assets, transitions and scene identifiers.
Keep the main experience first-person on-foot Mars observation.
Do not implement Rover operation in Phase 2; it is a possible optional feature after Day 14 and essential testing.
Drone operation is a separate later feature controlled from Mission Control; do not implement it in Days 1-5.
Keep the 14-day mission plan intact and do not invent additional modules.

player_perspective.description: During outdoor Mars observation, show the world through a lightweight astronaut-helmet visor treatment: mostly clear centre, darkened curved/circular edges, subtle vignette and restrained telemetry. Do not show a third-person astronaut body.
player_perspective.activation: Active for outdoor Master Terrain exploration. It must not incorrectly cover loading screens, destination videos, menus or other full-screen transitions. Inspect actual scene/transition state before implementing activation.

requirements: Preserve current controls where practical and document actual bindings discovered in the repository.
Reasonable walking pace and controlled acceleration/deceleration only if compatible with the existing controller.
Reliable ground detection and collision against actual terrain and relevant solid geometry.
No camera floating, falling through ground or passing through walls where collision is supported.
Do not assume one Three.js world unit equals one metre without checking scale.
Do not add a physics engine solely for this phase.
Avoid exaggerated head bob, motion blur or effects that hinder observation.
out_of_scope: Rover driving, wheel rotation, axle movement, suspension, wheel-by-wheel terrain following or Rover control UI.
Oxygen depletion, survival timers, player health or complex life-support simulation.

visual_system.style: Consistent, restrained science-fiction research expedition; legible, practical, not overly neon or cluttered.
principles: Reuse existing UI components, fonts, colours, layout conventions and visual references wherever present.
Do not redesign the entire app.
Prioritise the 3D scene and central observation area.
Keep HUD text compact and readable at common desktop resolutions.
Make primary action, secondary information, warnings and completion states visually distinguishable.
Provide responsive fallback behaviour if the app already supports different viewport sizes.
visual_system.reference_policy: Inspect all relevant screenshots and existing UI in the repository. If a screen has an explicit reference, follow it. If no reference exists, derive a minimal layout from the existing design system and this specification, documenting assumptions rather than inventing an elaborate new design.

data_integrity: Clearly distinguish simulated mission telemetry from real measurements.
Never claim PHOBOSIA is connected to live NASA systems unless that connection exists and is verified.
Do not invent scientific readings, terrain elevations, coordinates, source datasets or discoveries.
Use existing terrain coordinates and exported Master Terrain. Do not regenerate or relocate terrain in this phase.
Use existing scene objects and interaction points; inspect before adding anything.
mission_state_rules: Current day and objective must survive module transitions.
Entering a module alone does not complete an objective unless explicitly defined.
Unrelated interactions must not complete the current objective.
Validate completion from explicit required actions/results, not proximity alone unless explicitly specified.
Day advancement is permitted only after the day's required objective is complete and the player uses the established Habitat rest/sleep action.
Prevent duplicate advancement from repeated key presses, overlapping triggers or duplicate listeners.
Explain what remains when the player tries to rest before completing the objective.
Store observation/checklist/route results in the existing mission state architecture, not a new backend.
Do not implement Day 15. Day 14 is the end of the main campaign in a later phase.

existing_identifiers_to_preserve_and_ver.instruction: Verify these against the actual scene/repository. Preserve exact spelling and case if present. Do not assume all are already imported or loaded. Do not create duplicates to compensate for a loading or reference bug.

mission_briefing.behaviour: Show at mission start or day transition using the existing briefing/transition UI if available. Do not create a separate full-screen flow if an equivalent one exists.

persistent_hud.behaviour: Keep unobtrusive. Hide or adapt it during loading screens and destination videos.

fields: equipment or power status when relevant
rules: Use verified existing simulated values or clearly labelled illustrative/simulated statuses.
Do not drain oxygen or implement survival failure mechanics.
Show only relevant concise indicators, not every value permanently.
Use alert severity only when a real simulated event exists.

states: in range: concise interaction label and control hint
interaction in progress: subtle feedback if needed
interaction_feedback.behaviour: Reuse the existing interaction architecture and prevent duplicate triggers/listeners.

rules: Show meaningful progress based on actual completed requirements.
Do not show arbitrary percentages if progress is only a single binary action; use a checklist or status label instead.
Completion must be tied to validated mission state.

mission_data_contract.purpose: Recommended conceptual data contract. Adapt names and types to the repository's conventions; do not create a duplicate mission system if a suitable one exists.
data_design_rules: Use stable IDs for missions, steps, interactions and records.
Separate mission definitions from runtime completion state.
Keep state updates deterministic and idempotent.
Use TypeScript types/unions compatible with the existing project.
Use only fields actually needed; this is not a requirement to create every field if equivalent existing state exists.
Days 6-14 must be addable through data/configuration and reusable validators without duplicating the mission engine.

screen_inventory.purpose: Explain the current day's context and what the player must do.

hierarchy: small PHOBOSIA/project identity if already present
Continue/Start action using existing UI conventions
avoid: long paragraphs covering the entire 14-day story
invented full-screen art when no asset exists

acceptance_criteria: The briefing matches the actual current day.
The primary objective is understandable without external documentation.
The screen does not advance the mission by itself.
It does not break the established loading and destination-video flow.

screen_inventory.screen_type: Overlay on the outdoor first-person 3D scene
screen_inventory.purpose: Frame outdoor observation as viewed through an astronaut helmet and show concise mission telemetry.

layout.center: Keep the central Mars terrain view clear.
layout.edges: Darkened circular/curved visor border and subtle vignette, implemented with a lightweight CSS overlay if practical.
layout.top_or_upper_corner: Compact day number and mission/status indicator.
layout.lower_or_side_area: Contextual interaction prompt only when the player is in range of a usable interaction.
layout.secondary_corner: Compact simulated suit/oxygen/equipment/communication statuses, showing only relevant values.
layout.notification_area: Small temporary notification region for verified simulated mission events.

data: verified or clearly labelled simulated telemetry
current interaction prompt if in range
acceptance_criteria: No third-person astronaut body is visible.
The centre remains readable for terrain observation.
The visor does not block pointer lock or movement input.
The overlay does not cover loading screens or destination videos.
Telemetry is not misrepresented as live real-world data.
No complex holographic 3D system is introduced just for decoration.

screen_inventory.purpose: Explain what can be interacted with and communicate the result.

layout.position: Use the existing interaction UI location. If none exists, choose a compact location that does not obstruct the centre of view.
layout.content: Short action name, relevant key hint discovered from current controls, and result/status.
layout.success: Brief success message with relevant result.
layout.blocked: Brief explanation of why the action is unavailable.

acceptance_criteria: Only appears for a real usable interaction.
Does not display prompts for decorative objects without interactions.
The same action cannot fire multiple times due to overlapping triggers.
Interaction results are recorded in mission state when relevant.

screen_inventory.purpose: Let the player understand what remains to complete the day.

layout.position: Use the current HUD/mission panel convention.
layout.content: Short objective title and required steps/checklist.
layout.progress: Use actual step completion or a simple status label; do not invent percentages.
layout.completion: Clear completion state and a concise instruction to return to Habitat to rest when appropriate.

acceptance_criteria: Progress reflects actual validated steps.
Incomplete steps remain visible.
Objective completion is not confused with permission to advance the day.
The player can still explore after completing the objective.

screen_inventory.screen_type: Existing Habitat rest/sleep interaction and feedback
screen_inventory.purpose: Allow the player to explicitly finish a day and start the next one after its objective is complete.

layout.interaction_prompt: Rest/Sleep or the equivalent existing interaction label.
layout.if_incomplete: Show that the current objective is incomplete and list or summarise remaining required steps.
layout.if_complete: Show a confirmation or concise transition feedback using the existing UI flow.

rules: Do not automatically advance time when an objective completes.
Day 5 must not advance to Day 6 unless the later campaign implementation supports it and the route-planning objective is validated.
acceptance_criteria: The rest interaction is explicit.
Incomplete objectives block advancement.
A successful rest advances the day exactly once.
Repeated inputs cannot skip days.
The next day's briefing and objective load correctly.

days.title: Base Orientation
days.purpose: Introduce the player to the base, first-person controls and established connected modules without an overly long tutorial.
days.story_context: The mission begins at the existing spawn point. The player receives an orientation briefing before beginning the first operational day.

start.spawn: Use the actual existing Day 1/start spawn configuration. Do not invent or move a spawn location.
start.briefing: Explain that the player is beginning a 14-day Mars observation mission and must become familiar with the base and its available work areas.

days.primary_objective: Complete a basic base-orientation checklist by visiting/inspecting designated existing orientation points.

required_steps.label: Review movement and interaction controls
required_steps.action: Show a concise control hint through the existing briefing or help UI.
required_steps.validation: The hint is displayed or acknowledged if existing UI supports acknowledgement. Do not require an elaborate tutorial system.

required_steps.label: Explore the Central Hub
required_steps.action: Player enters or inspects the existing Central Hub orientation point.
required_steps.validation: Use a real existing trigger or explicit interaction. Do not assume mere module loading is an objective unless designed as such.

required_steps.label: Identify the main work areas
required_steps.action: Visit a small set of existing designated orientation points in modules that are already connected and accessible.
required_steps.validation: Use only actual existing modules and interaction points. Do not require every module if that creates excessive backtracking.

required_steps.label: Confirm base orientation
required_steps.action: Use the existing orientation confirmation interaction or a minimal interaction in the current system.
required_steps.validation: Only complete after required orientation steps are recorded.

allowed_locations: Existing connected modules that are accessible in the current build

must_show: Concise movement/interaction controls based on actual bindings
Each required step and actual status

days.completion_rule: All required Day 1 orientation steps must be validated. Completion enables the Habitat rest action; it does not automatically advance the day.
days.completion_feedback: Show a concise confirmation that base orientation is complete and the player may continue exploring or return to the Habitat to rest.
failure_and_edge_cases: Re-entering a module must not duplicate progress.
A decorative object must not satisfy a required step.
If a designated interaction point is missing, report it rather than silently inventing a new scene object.
Do not make optional module exploration mandatory.
acceptance_criteria: Day 1 is represented as data in the existing mission architecture.
The briefing and checklist reflect actual mission state.
The objective completes only after validated steps.
The player can freely explore after completing the objective.
The player cannot advance the day before completion.
Rest advances to Day 2 exactly once.

days.title: Habitat Readiness
days.purpose: Perform a straightforward simulated readiness check using existing Habitat equipment and interaction points.
days.story_context: After initial orientation, the player verifies that the Habitat is ready for the next observation activities.

start.spawn: Use established day-transition spawn/placement behaviour. Do not invent a new spawn point.
start.briefing: Explain that the player must inspect existing Habitat readiness items and confirm their status.

days.primary_objective: Inspect designated existing Habitat readiness interaction(s) and record the result.

required_steps.label: Enter the Habitat
required_steps.action: Use the existing Habitat entrance and transition.
required_steps.validation: Verify the actual Habitat trigger and destination transition.

required_steps.label: Inspect Habitat readiness
required_steps.action: Interact with actual existing equipment/interaction point(s) that can reasonably represent readiness.
required_steps.validation: Reuse existing interaction objects. If none exists, add the smallest interaction supported by the existing system and document the exact object/reference used.

required_steps.label: Record readiness status
required_steps.action: Confirm a concise simulated readiness checklist/result.
required_steps.validation: Store the result in mission state. Do not imply live telemetry.

must_show: Instruction to inspect designated Habitat interaction point(s)
Clear feedback if relevant equipment interaction is unavailable

out_of_scope: Making HAB_WORKSTATION_01 entertainment a required objective
days.completion_rule: Required Habitat readiness interaction(s) are complete and the result is recorded. The player must explicitly rest in the Habitat to advance to Day 3.
days.completion_feedback: Show a clear readiness result and explain that the objective is complete.
acceptance_criteria: Day 2 can be completed using actual accessible interactions.
The checklist contains no invented sensor values.
The result persists across module transitions.
HAB_WORKSTATION_01 and its existing relationships remain intact.
Rest advances to Day 3 exactly once.

days.title: Power System Observation
days.purpose: Record a simple simulated observation of the base power system using existing Engineering and solar-panel assets.
days.story_context: The player performs a baseline power-system observation before more demanding outdoor science work.

start.briefing: Explain that the player must inspect the designated power-system observation point and record the displayed simulated status.

days.primary_objective: Inspect the existing power-related interaction point and save a baseline observation record.

required_steps.label: Reach the Engineering Unit
required_steps.action: Use the existing Engineering entrance transition.

required_steps.label: Inspect the power system
required_steps.action: Use an existing power-system or solar-panel interaction point if one is available.
required_steps.validation: Inspect actual loaded assets and interaction references. Do not assume solar panels are interactive just because they are visible.

required_steps.label: Record the baseline observation
required_steps.action: Save a small observation record with source/interaction identifier, mission day, timestamp if the project already supports it, and clearly labelled simulated status/result.
required_steps.validation: Use only existing data or intentionally defined simulated data. Do not invent real electrical measurements.

allowed_locations: Existing outdoor solar-panel area if already accessible

must_show: Source equipment/interaction label based on actual assets
screen_requirements.design_rule: Use an existing panel or contextual interaction result. Do not create a large new dashboard if a compact panel satisfies the task.

must_show: Contextual observation prompt near a usable interaction point
Compact equipment status only if relevant

data_rules: Clearly label simulated readings or statuses.
Do not claim connection to real solar-panel telemetry.
Preserve existing solar-panel assets, transforms and names.
days.completion_rule: The player has completed the required power observation and the result has been recorded in mission state.
days.completion_feedback: Confirm that the baseline observation was recorded and allow free exploration before the player rests.
acceptance_criteria: The Engineering transition works.
The power observation is an actual interaction rather than a decorative prompt.
A result is stored and can be referenced by later mission logic.
The UI makes simulated data clear.
Rest advances to Day 4 exactly once.

days.title: Life-Support Verification
days.purpose: Perform a concise simulated life-support readiness verification using existing Habitat and Engineering equipment.
days.story_context: The player checks relevant life-support readiness before beginning the outdoor scientific survey sequence.

start.briefing: Explain that the player must inspect relevant existing life-support interaction point(s), review the simulated result and record the verification.

days.primary_objective: Complete a simple life-support readiness verification and save its result.

required_steps.label: Reach the relevant equipment
required_steps.action: Use existing Habitat and/or Engineering transitions based on the actual equipment placement.
required_steps.validation: Determine equipment location by inspecting the actual scene and code. Do not assume a new object exists.

required_steps.label: Inspect life-support readiness
required_steps.action: Interact with the actual available relevant equipment point.
required_steps.validation: Use the existing interaction system or a minimal extension. Do not add resource depletion or survival mechanics.

required_steps.label: Record the verification result
required_steps.action: Save the result in mission state with a clear simulated status label.
required_steps.validation: Only mark complete after the result is stored successfully.

must_show: Location hint based on actual equipment placement
A warning only if an actual simulated event is defined

days.completion_rule: The required verification interaction has been completed and its result saved. The player must explicitly rest in the Habitat to advance.
days.completion_feedback: Show the verification result and explain that the objective is complete.
acceptance_criteria: The interaction uses actual available equipment or a documented minimal addition.
Day 2 and Day 4 reuse shared interaction and checklist logic where practical.
The result is persisted in mission state.
No survival mechanics are introduced.
Rest advances to Day 5 exactly once.

days.title: Terrain Route Planning
days.purpose: Prepare for upcoming Mars terrain observations using the existing Master Terrain and Mission Control.
days.story_context: Before the first major outdoor survey, the player reviews the established observation area and records a practical route plan.

start.briefing: Explain that the player must review the existing observation area and confirm a route or target selection for the next scientific activity.

days.primary_objective: Review the existing terrain/map representation, select or confirm a route/observation target using available UI, and save the plan.

required_steps.label: Reach Mission Control
required_steps.action: Use the existing Mission Control entrance transition.

required_steps.label: Review the existing observation area
required_steps.action: Use the actual available map or terrain representation. Preserve selected location and existing terrain coordinates.
required_steps.validation: Inspect current map UI and terrain data. Do not invent coordinates, route lengths, slopes, elevation or geographic labels.

required_steps.label: Select or confirm the observation route/target
required_steps.action: Reuse an existing route-selection interface if available. Otherwise implement a minimal, clear selection/confirmation UI compatible with the current project.
required_steps.validation: The selected target must correspond to a real existing marker, supported map coordinate or verified scene location. Do not place arbitrary new markers without documenting why.

required_steps.label: Save the route plan
required_steps.action: Save the selected target/route reference in mission state.
required_steps.validation: Only mark the step complete after a valid selection is saved.

must_show: Why planning is needed before outdoor observation
Instruction to review the existing map/terrain in Mission Control
Actual existing map or terrain preview if available
Selectable existing targets or supported route choices
Validation feedback if no valid target is selected

layout_guidance.preferred: Reuse existing Mission Control map/planning layout. Keep map/terrain preview as the main visual region and route/target controls in a compact side panel if the current design supports that pattern.
layout_guidance.fallback: If no planning screen exists, create a simple responsive panel using existing visual components. Do not create a new 3D map or external mapping dependency without need.
not_allowed: Unverified distances, slope measurements or elevation values

must_show: Confirmation that the plan was saved
Short note that the plan supports the upcoming observation mission

data_rules: Use current Master Terrain and its existing coordinates.
Do not regenerate or relocate the terrain.
Do not claim a selected route is scientifically optimal unless the application calculates and validates that.
If no existing route data or markers are available, implement a minimal selection mechanism grounded in actual terrain references and document it.
days.completion_rule: A valid existing target/route has been selected and the route plan is saved. The player must return to the Habitat and explicitly rest to advance when the next-day mission is implemented.
days.completion_feedback: Confirm the route plan was saved and explain that the player may continue exploring or rest when ready.
acceptance_criteria: Mission Control transition works.
Planning UI uses actual terrain data and existing references.
Selection is saved in mission state.
Invalid/no selection prevents completion.
Route plan is available for later mission logic.
No Day 6 geological survey gameplay is implemented in Phase 2.
Existing coordinates and terrain assets remain unchanged.

expected_sequence: Start the current day and display its briefing.
Show contextual prompts only near valid interactions.
Validate each required step and store its result.
Display objective completion feedback when all requirements are satisfied.
Allow free exploration after objective completion.
Require explicit Habitat rest/sleep interaction to advance the day.
If requirements are incomplete, block advancement and explain what remains.
Advance to the next day exactly once and show the next briefing.
cross_day_flow.important_distinction: Objective completion and day advancement are separate states. Completing an objective does not automatically start the next day.
cross_day_flow.implementation_note: Use existing state conventions if they differ. Do not introduce redundant parallel state machines.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Project builds and starts using its existing commands.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Actual build/start commands complete successfully or failures are documented precisely.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Outdoor first-person movement works on the existing Master Terrain.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Player can walk without falling through or floating above actual terrain, within the limits of the current collision system.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Helmet visor activates only in the intended outdoor state.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Visible outdoors and does not incorrectly cover loading screens, videos or other full-screen UI.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Mission day and objective remain consistent across module transitions.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Changing modules does not reset or accidentally advance the day.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Day 1 orientation can be completed through validated interactions.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Only required orientation steps complete the objective.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Day 2 Habitat readiness can be completed.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Checklist uses real implemented interactions and saves the result.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Day 3 power observation can be completed.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Baseline simulated observation is recorded and clearly labelled.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Day 4 life-support verification can be completed.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Result is recorded without adding survival mechanics.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Day 5 route planning can be completed.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: A valid existing terrain target/route reference is saved; invalid selection is blocked.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Rest cannot advance an incomplete day.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: A clear blocked message is shown and current day remains unchanged.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Rest advances a completed day exactly once.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Repeated inputs and trigger overlap cannot skip a day.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Existing entrance triggers continue to work.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Engineering, Habitat, AirLock, Mission Control and Science Lab transitions are tested and outcomes documented.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Known scene objects and assets remain intact.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Existing identifiers and relationships are verified against the real scene; no accidental renames or duplicate objects.

phase_2_acceptance_tests.description: Simulated telemetry and notifications are truthful.
phase_2_acceptance_tests.pass_condition: UI does not imply a real live connection or invent actual NASA telemetry.
Screens follow existing visual references and design conventions; layout and key states are checked at the target desktop viewport.

required_sections: Mission data model and state progression
Existing triggers and scene object verification
Tests passed, failed, not run, and manual checks required
Known limitations and unresolved asset/interaction dependencies
Recommended next phase based on the established 14-day plan
implementation_reporting.truthfulness_rule: Never report a visual, gameplay, interaction or transition test as passed unless it was actually executed and verified. Distinguish code inspection from runtime verification.
